newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria August industrial output up 2.0 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria August industrial output up 2.0 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Bulgarian industrial output rose by a real 2.0 percent in August against the same month last year, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.
BULGARIA STATE INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT AUG JULY AUG'95
Industrial production in the state sector amounted to 135 billion levs in current prices in August and totalled 676 billion levs for the first eight months of 1996.

Output rose most in the chemical and oil-processing industries in the first eight months, while metallurgy, printing industry, food and beverage industry and pulp and paper production posted a decline compared to the same period of 1995, the NSI said.
Industrial output in both the state and the private sector amounted to 156 billion levs in current prices in August, up a real 3.0 percent year-on-year.
For the first eight months of the year the total industrial output in the two sectors rose a real 1.0 percent year-on-year to 784 billion levs in current prices, NSI figures showed.

"Although we have registered some increase in industrial production in August, economic climate remains rather unfavourable for producers and a decline could be expected in the months ahead," a NSI official told a news conference.
Demand continues to be rather low and many enterprises are burdened with rising debts, while high interest rates on credits deter producers from fresh borrowing, the official added.
The rise in output in the private industrial sector in August slowed down to a real 10 percent year-on-year from some 30 percent until May, the NSI said.
The private industrial sector in Bulgaria accounted for some 14 percent of total output during the first eight months of this year.
